newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's El-Op unveils advanced laser for U.S..
newsitem.headline: Israel's El-Op unveils advanced laser for U.S..

text.p: Israel's Electro-Optics Industries Ltd (El-Op) unveiled on Sunday an innovative laser guidance system for the next-generation U.S. Commanche attack helicopter.

The laser system, which is unnamed, operates on two different spectral wavelengths -- one used for directing laser-guided weapons and the other for gathering range data during training and combat operations, said Gil Wiener, project manager for the system at El-Op.

Utilising solid state devices and advanced optics, the El-Op laser enables data-gathering at a wavelength that does not cause damage to the eyes, as is often the case with laser rangefinders, Weiner said.
The new system employs new technology called diode-pump, which increases its efficiency and lowers power consumption, making the unit lighter.

El-Op, a maker of electro-optic systems for defence applications, was chosen in 1992 to develop laser systems for the electronics and missiles unit of the U.S. defence contractor Lockheed-Martin Corp.
Lockheed is developing targeting and navigation capabilities for the Commanche. Boeing/Sikorsky, the main contractor, will ultimately produce 1,200 of the aircraft for the U.S. Army.
Full production is not expected to begin until the year 2006, but between now and 1998, Lockheed officials said they would be ordering at least eight systems from El-Op.

In the meantime, El-Op president Jacob Toren said he expected the technology would be used elsewhere. "The diode-pump upgrades will be put on the Apache and other platforms before the first six (Comanches)," he said. El-Op already supplies laser systems for the Apache, another attack helicopter.
The two companies would not reveal the price of the laser, which is still under negotiation, but Toren indicated it would be under $100,000.

El-Op, a closely held company, expects to have revenues of $270 million this year, about 15 percent from lasers. Aviv Haleva, a spokesman, would not reveal earnings but said the company had been consistently profitable over the last seven years.
She said that even in an era of declining defence spending, the success of allied forces in the 1991 Gulf War using electro-optics, like night-vision equipment, has created demand for El-Op products.
